page_title: objekto.io — AI design and 3D printing of custom objects, delivered in France

sources.entry: objekto.io - Turns a few words, a photo or a sketch into a multi-part, print-ready 3D model designed by AI, then has it 3D printed and delivered (France only for now). #freemium

summary.name: objekto
summary.one_liner: objekto is a French online service that turns a text description, photo, sketch or 3D file into an AI-designed, multi-part 3D model that is industrially printed and delivered to your door.
keywords: design a custom object from a description
make a custom object from a photo
use_cases: Design a custom object from a text description
Turn a photo or sketch into a printable 3D model
Get a multi-part object 3D printed and delivered in France
Create a replacement or custom part with assembly guide
Prototype a toy or household item
summary.what_it_does: The service uses AI to design a 3D model from a few words, a photo, a sketch or a 3D file, working part by part. It checks each part for print-readiness (wall thickness per material, maximum machine size, clearances, watertight mesh, stability) and splits large objects into parts with printed joints. It shows an exploded view and a step-by-step PDF assembly guide. Parts are then made by an industrial 3D-printing workshop in materials such as PETG, PLA, PA12 nylon, TPU/TPE, resin or metal, and delivered; the page states that a live price is shown and the AI chooses materials within the user's budget.
notable: Credit-based AI design: 4,300 free credits on signup, enough for a 2-4 part object, no card needed
Splits large objects into parts with printed joints, exploded view and PDF assembly guide
Automatic checks for wall thickness, clearance, watertight mesh and stability before manufacturing
Max 16 unique parts per object in v1, depending on plan
caveats: Delivery is France only for now
Printed objects are not certified for food contact, medical use or load-bearing applications
Manufacturing and delivery take about 1 to 3 weeks; printing is paid in US dollars
Designs are public by default in Explore; can be made private
